title: Built to Stand
description: Bridges, machines and the ideas that keep ambitious structures working.

questions.prompt: What do engineers call a force that squeezes a structural member along its length?
questions.hint: Think about the difference between pushing a spring together and pulling it apart.
questions.explanation: Compression squeezes a member; tension pulls it apart. Torsion twists and shear tends to slide adjacent parts past each other.

questions.prompt: Why do many truss bridges use triangles in their framework?

choices.text: They keep every structural member horizontal
They ensure that no member carries tension
A triangle with fixed side lengths keeps its shape
They remove the need for end supports

questions.hint: Compare a hinged triangle with a hinged rectangle made from rigid bars.
questions.explanation: A triangle cannot change shape without changing a side length. An unbraced four-sided frame can distort at its joints.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Verified geometrically by side-side-side rigidity, assuming rigid members joined at their ends; does not claim a real triangle has infinite strength.

questions.prompt: In a hydroelectric dam, flowing water first turns which machine to drive a generator?
questions.hint: Follow the transfer from moving water to a rotating shaft.
questions.explanation: Water turns a turbine connected to a generator, which converts the shaft’s mechanical energy into electricity.

questions.prompt: Why are expansion joints included in many bridges?

choices.text: To increase the span after each crossing
To prevent corrosion of every steel part
To allow movement as temperature changes

questions.hint: A structure’s dimensions are not quite the same on a hot day and a cold day.
questions.explanation: Bridge materials expand and contract with temperature. Joints accommodate movement that would otherwise create damaging stresses.

questions.prompt: The main cables of a conventional suspension bridge carry their load primarily through what?
questions.hint: A flexible cable behaves differently when you pull its ends apart than when you push them together.
questions.explanation: The cables are pulled taut, carrying tensile forces that transfer the deck load toward towers and anchorages.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Checked cable/tension distinction in structural bridge research; question concerns flexible main cables, not towers or deck.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes a simple cantilever beam?

choices.text: It must curve into an arch
It is fixed at one end and free at the other
It hangs from cables at both ends
It rests only on a central roller

questions.hint: A projecting balcony provides a familiar example of this support arrangement.
questions.explanation: A cantilever projects from a fixed support, which resists both force and turning effect at that end.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the counterweight in a traction elevator?

choices.text: To increase friction between the cabin and its guides
To set the cabin’s stopping point at each floor
To reduce the load imbalance the motor must move
To absorb impacts when the cabin reaches the bottom

questions.hint: Consider the effort needed to raise one side of a nearly balanced system.
questions.explanation: The counterweight balances much of the cabin and load, reducing the effort and energy required from the drive.

questions.prompt: An ideal hydraulic press has an output piston with four times the input piston’s area. How does its output force compare with the input force?

choices.text: It is one quarter as large
It is four times as large

questions.hint: Pressure is force divided by area; the liquid transmits the pressure change.
questions.explanation: Equal pressure acting over four times the area gives four times the force. The larger piston moves a correspondingly shorter distance.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Verified Fout/Aout=Fin/Ain, Aout=4Ain ->Fout=4Fin. Ideal system stated; pressure difference and energy conservation both respected.

questions.prompt: Why is steel reinforcement useful on the tension side of a concrete beam?

choices.text: Concrete is relatively weak in tension
Steel prevents the beam from having any weight

questions.hint: Different materials can complement one another rather than perform identical jobs.
questions.explanation: Concrete carries compression well but is weak in tension. Steel reinforcement can carry tensile forces where bending stretches the beam.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Checked ACI Education Bulletin E2-00 section 2.2.1 on concrete's low tensile strength and steel reinforcement resisting beam-action tension; qualified wording avoids saying reinforcement prevents all cracking.

questions.prompt: A long, slender column suddenly bows sideways under a compressive load. What instability is this?
questions.hint: Failure need not begin with the material being crushed; geometry also matters.
questions.explanation: Buckling is a loss of stability under compression. A slender column can bend sideways before its material reaches its crushing strength.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Checked flexural buckling and Euler-load discussion; gradual creep and cyclic fatigue are deliberately distinct distractors.

questions.prompt: What does prestressing deliberately introduce into a concrete member before its full service load acts?
questions.hint: The aim is to offset the kind of stress that would otherwise open cracks.
questions.explanation: Tensioned steel tendons apply compression to the concrete. Later load-induced tension must first overcome that initial compression.

questions.prompt: The large suspended mass inside Taipei 101 is designed chiefly to do what?

choices.text: Lift water to the top floors

questions.hint: A secondary moving system can exchange energy with a swaying structure.
questions.explanation: The tuned mass damper moves relative to the building and works with damping devices to reduce its vibration.

questions.prompt: A simply supported beam’s span doubles while its uniform load per metre stays unchanged. How does the maximum bending moment change?

choices.text: It becomes four times as large
It becomes eight times as large

questions.hint: Consider both the increase in total load and the increase in the distances over which forces act.
questions.explanation: The peak bending moment is wL²/8 for uniform load w and span L. Doubling L therefore multiplies it by four.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Independent statics derivation: each reaction=wL/2; at centre M=(wL/2)(L/2)-(wL/2)(L/4)=wL²/8. Substitution2L gives factor4. This is a specialist load-scaling question, not just a formula-substitution exercise.

questions.prompt: An ideal flexible cable carries a vertical load uniform per metre of horizontal span, with its own weight neglected. What curve does it form between its supports?
questions.hint: Distinguish a load distributed along the horizontal span from the cable’s own weight distributed along its length.
questions.explanation: A uniform load per horizontal distance gives a parabolic cable. A uniform cable hanging under only its own weight instead forms a catenary.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Checked exact load assumption; catenary and parabola are not treated as interchangeable.

questions.prompt: A beam is fixed at one end and propped by a roller at the other. For its small elastic deflection under load, what is needed in addition to force and moment equilibrium to find all support reactions?

choices.text: Only the total mass of the beam
A condition that deflection at the prop is zero
A rule that both vertical reactions are equal
A condition that the fixed-end moment is zero

questions.hint: The extra support constrains a displacement as well as supplying a force.
questions.explanation: The propped cantilever is statically indeterminate. Its zero deflection at the prop supplies a compatibility condition, used with the beam’s elastic behaviour.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Checked propped cantilever indeterminacy; equilibrium has fewer independent equations than reaction unknowns. Linear-elastic small-deflection context stated; the fixed support can resist a nonzero moment.
